newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Retail investors line up for Vedior subscription.
newsitem.headline: Retail investors line up for Vedior subscription.

text.p: Lured by a booming bourse and a well-known brand-name in a growth sector, Dutch retail investors are fighting for shares in employment services group Vedior, to float on the Amsterdam Exchanges on June 5.

"People started to call last Thursday already, when the subscription wasn't even open yet," said Dejan Markovic, an employee of the Postbank's bourse order line, a telephone service aimed mainly at retail customers.
He said interest in Vedior shares was more marked than in Dutch feeds group Nutreco, also to be floated next week.

"Many read in this weekend's newspaper the Nutreco- subscription would close today at 0900 GMT so there was a run on Nutreco shares this morning, but on Friday, Vedior was definitely the number one," Markovic said.
A Rabobank Nederland spokesman said on Friday afternoon the close of the subscription in Nutreco shares for retail investors had been brought forward from June 2 due to high retail demand.
"Interest among retail investors has been extremely high and we do not want to disappoint applicants," said Jan van Schaik.
Retail brokers said the Vedior listing was likely to create even more enthusiasm.
"There has been a lot of interest in all bourse listings recently, but the interest in Vedior is really big," said an employee of KBW Effectenbank who asked not be identified.
"It's far bigger than in Nutreco, to me it seems more comparable with Endemol," he said.
Shares in Dutch television production company Endemol Entertainment NV were first listed on the Amsterdam stock Exchange on November 1 of last year.
The Endemol offering closed more than one week early, with the issue 25 times over-subscribed.
"People are convinced the Vedior issue will be heavily oversubscribed, so they subscribe to more shares than they actually want," Markovic said.
Markovic said the bourse order line of the Postbank, a banking unit of ING, had installed a special seven-man team to handle retail customers' queries on Vedior.

The KBW employee said the size of the Vedior subscriptions was larger than the average orders the bank got from retail customers. "One shouldn't think of a couple of hundred shares, it's mostly more than that, he said.
"It goes from some hundreds to several thousands of shares," Markovic said. He said he was 90 percent sure the Vedior subscription would close earlier than planned.
"And then, we'll have to divide among our subscribers whatever number of shares we got attributed by the lead, however difficult that may be," said the KBW employee.
16,713,810 certificates of ordinary shares in Vedior N.V. and possibly an additional issue of 2,507,000 certificates will be offered at between 33 and 37 guilders per share.
Vedior is an offshoot of retail and business services group Vendex International.

With almost 80 percent of sales generated in temporary employment services and 20 percent in cleaning, Vedior derives 62 percent of its sales from France, 23 percent from the Netherlands and 12 of Belgium and Luxemburg.
"In temporary employment, we're number three in Europe; in cleaning, we're number two," Vedior chairman Gert Smit told reporters on Thursday.
Vedior had pro-forma sales in the fiscal year 1996/97 of 6.5 billion guilders, with operating income of 221 million guilders.
